mainTopic: Offering outside the עזרה (העלאה בחוץ), and when an עולה's meat and אימורים combine to a כזית
overview: The משנה teaches that a person is liable for offering קדשים outside the Temple courtyard. This is true both for fit offerings and for offerings that became unfit inside the holy area. It also teaches that a כזית made of עולה meat together with its אימורים adds up to make him liable. A ברייתא learns these rules from the פסוק in ויקרא 17 in three layers. עולה teaches the burnt offering, זבח adds the אימורים of all other offerings, and פתח אהל מועד adds the קומץ, קטורת, מנחות and נסכים. The words לא יביאנו לעשות then add פסולין that the altar would accept. Next the גמרא reads the משנה closely: only an עולה's meat and אימורים combine, not those of שלמים. A ברייתא says the same and adds that they combine for פיגול, נותר and טמא. The גמרא challenges this from a משנה that says all פיגול and all נותר combine. It answers that the ברייתא is about the thought that makes פיגול, and about a case where only a כזית was left before the blood was sprinkled. It says this ברייתא follows רבי יהושע and begins quoting his ruling, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Fit and unfit offerings sacrificed outside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person who offers קדשים outside the courtyard is liable, whether the offerings were fit or became unfit inside the holy area.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Whether the offerings were fit, or they were unfit but became unfit inside the holy area, if someone offered them outside, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a rule: offering קדשים outside the עזרה makes a person liable. This is true even for offerings that became פסול inside the holy area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think an offering that is already unfit no longer counts as a real offering, so offering it outside would not matter. The משנה says that if it became unfit inside the קודש, it still counts, and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'
Offerings that are fit
Offerings that became unfit
In the holy area (inside the Temple)
Outside the Temple courtyard
Liable (to punishment)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying that every unfit offering makes you liable. It covers only offerings whose disqualification happened inside the קודש.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Both fit sacrificial animals
and unfit sacrificial animals
whose disqualification happened in the holy area
and he offered them outside: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד קֳדָשִׁים כְּשֵׁרִין וְאֶחָד קָדָשִׁים פְּסוּלִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering קדשים outside makes a person liable, both for fit offerings and for offerings that became unfit inside the קודש.

steps.title: An olive-bulk made of meat and sacrificial portions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a כזית made partly of עולה meat and partly of אימורים, offered outside, makes a person liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who offers up outside an olive-bulk made from the burnt offering and from the sacrificial portions is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule. Two different parts of offerings can join together to make the minimum amount, a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount that makes a person liable is a כזית. Here the עולה meat and the אימורים are both parts that go on the מזבח, so together they add up to the required amount.

keyTerms.meaning: One who offers up (burns on an altar)
An olive-bulk, the minimum amount
Burnt offering, entirely burned on the altar
Sacrificial portions burned on the altar

phrases.english: One who offers up an olive-bulk
from the burnt offering and from the sacrificial portions
outside is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּעֲלֶה כְּזַיִת מִן הָעוֹלָה וּמִן הָאֵימוּרִין בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rule in the same משנה, about combining parts to reach a כזית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כזית made of עולה meat and אימורים together makes a person liable when he offers it outside.

steps.title: The verse mentions only a burnt offering: what about other sacrificial portions?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק about offering outside. It notes that the word עולה alone would teach only a burnt offering, and asks how we know the אימורים of other offerings are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Sages taught: "That offers up a burnt offering or sacrifice." From this I would know only about a burnt offering. From where do we include the portions of a guilt offering, a sin offering, most sacred offerings, and offerings of lesser sanctity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts reading the פסוק word by word. It is setting up a question that the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely, so it is the clearest case. Other offerings have only some parts, the אימורים, burned on the מזבח. The ברייתא asks which word in the פסוק covers those parts.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know
From where do we include?
Guilt offering
Sin offering
Offerings of lesser sanctity

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
"That offers up a burnt offering or sacrifice"
I would only know about a burnt offering;
from where do we include the sacrificial portions of a guilt offering,
and the sacrificial portions of a sin offering,
and the sacrificial portions of the most sacred offerings,
and the sacrificial portions of offerings of lesser sanctity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins finding the source in the פסוק for the משנה's rules
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which word in the פסוק includes the אימורים of offerings other than an עולה?

steps.title: The word 'sacrifice' includes all sacrificial portions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the word זבח in the פסוק includes the אימורים of all other offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The extra word זבח adds the burned parts of all other offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולה covers an offering that is burned completely. זבח covers offerings where only the אימורים go on the מזבח. Now both kinds are included.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the answer from a פסוק)
Sacrifice, an offering that is not entirely burned

phrases.english: The verse says: "sacrifice."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word זבח includes the אימורים of אשם, חטאת, קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים.

steps.title: What about the handful, incense, priestly meal offerings, and libations?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know a person is liable for offering outside items that are not animal parts: the קומץ, לבונה, קטורת, the priests' מנחות, and the wine and water נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we include the handful, the frankincense, the incense, the priests' meal offering, the anointed priest's meal offering, and one who pours three לוגין of wine or three לוגין of water?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to a new question about items that are not animal offerings at all. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולה and זבח are both animal offerings. The question is whether things like flour, spices, and liquids that go on the מזבח also make a person liable when he offers them outside.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה and burned
Frankincense
Incense
The כהן גדול's daily meal offering
One who pours a libation
A liquid measure (plural of לוג)

phrases.english: From where do we include the handful,
and the frankincense, and the incense,
and the meal offering of priests, and the meal offering of the anointed priest,
and one who pours three log of wine,
and three log of water?
phrases.notes: This is the water poured on the מזבח on סוכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the question from animal parts to all things offered on the מזבח
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which source makes a person liable for offering non-animal items such as the קומץ, קטורת, מנחות and נסכים outside?

steps.title: Anything brought to the Tent of Meeting is included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the phrase פתח אהל מועד that a person is liable for offering outside anything that would be brought to the entrance of the אהל מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And he will not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting." Anything that comes to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, one is liable for it outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a broad rule from the פסוק. Anything that belongs on the מזבח inside makes a person liable if he offers it outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of listing items one by one, the פסוק gives a general test: was this item meant to be brought to פתח אהל מועד? If so, offering it outside is forbidden, and that covers all the items in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance of the Tent of Meeting
He will not bring it
One is liable for it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three layers of inclusion from the פסוק. עולה teaches the burnt offering. זבח adds the אימורים of all other offerings. פתח אהל מועד adds every item brought to the מזבח, including flour, spices, and liquids.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the general test for offering outside (העלאה בחוץ): liability depends on whether the item belongs on the מזבח inside, not on whether it is an animal. Step 8 widens this test to cover unfit offerings too.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And he will not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting"
anything that comes to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
one is liable for it outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְאֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לֹא יְבִיאֶנּוּ״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase פתח אהל מועד includes anything fit to be brought to the מזבח, so one is liable for offering it outside.

steps.title: What about offerings that became unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know a person is liable for offering outside even קדשים that became פסול, and lists many examples of such offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far we only know about fit offerings. How do we know to include unfit ones? For example: meat left overnight, an offering that went outside the courtyard, an impure offering, one slaughtered with intent for outside its time or place, one whose blood unfit people collected and sprinkled, blood meant for below the red line that was put above it, blood meant for above it that was put below, blood meant for outside that was put inside, blood meant for inside that was put outside, and a פסח or חטאת done not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a new question. Fine, a kosher offering offered outside makes you liable, but what about an offering that was already ruined (פסול)?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think: if the offering is already פסול, it is not a real קרבן anymore, so offering it outside is not a sin. The ברייתא lists the kinds of פסול it is asking about. They all became פסול after they were already holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings that became unfit
Offering meat that was left overnight past its time
An offering that went outside its allowed area
Slaughtered with intent to eat or offer it after its time or outside its place
Done not for the sake of the offering it really is

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about every kind of פסול. It is about these specific kinds, where the offering became unfit while it was already holy, and the answer in the next step depends on that.

phrases.english: I have only fit offerings;
phrases.notes: He means: so far, our sources only taught liability for kosher offerings.

phrases.english: from where do we include unfit ones?
for example, what was left overnight, what went out, and what is impure,
and one slaughtered beyond its time or outside its place,
and one where unfit people collected and sprinkled its blood,
and blood meant to be placed below that one placed above,
phrases.notes: Below or above the red line that ran around the מזבח.

phrases.english: and blood meant to be placed above that one placed below,
and blood meant to be placed outside that one placed inside,
and blood meant to be placed inside that one placed outside,
and a Pesach or sin offering placed not for their own sake –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא קֳדָשִׁים כְּשֵׁרִים; מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת פְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After including non-animal items in Step 6, the ברייתא now asks about a new group: offerings that became פסול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that offering disqualified קדשים outside still makes a person liable.

steps.title: Anything the altar accepts makes you liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the words לא יביאנו לעשות that anything the altar at the entrance of the אהל מועד would accept makes a person liable if he offers it outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where? The verse says: 'He will not bring it to offer.' This teaches that for anything that is accepted at the entrance of the אהל מועד, a person is liable if he offers it outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question about unfit offerings. The test is not whether the offering is perfect. The test is whether the altar would accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listed פסולין became unfit while already holy, so if they were put on the altar, the altar would 'accept' them. Because they count as accepted inside, offering them outside makes a person liable. The key is the word מתקבל.

keyTerms.meaning: What is accepted (by the altar)
To offer (literally, to do), the word that adds offerings the altar accepts

steps.whatToRemember: The rule for offering outside: if the altar inside would accept it, offering it outside makes you liable, even if it is פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a broad rule (whatever is מתקבל inside) that measures liability outside, instead of a list of single cases.

phrases.english: From where? The verse states:
'He will not bring it to offer' –
anything that is accepted at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
one is liable for it outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: לֹא יְבִיאֶנּוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase לא יביאנו לעשות includes anything that is מתקבל at the entrance of the אהל מועד, so disqualified offerings that the altar accepts still make a person liable outside.

steps.title: Close reading of the משנה: עולה yes, שלמים no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about a כזית from an עולה and its אימורים. It infers that this works only for an עולה, not for שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who offers up an olive-bulk from the burnt offering, etc.' A burnt offering and its sacrificial parts, yes; a peace offering and its sacrificial parts, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and reads it closely to draw an inference. This sets up the next move in the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of an עולה's meat is burned on the altar, so its meat and its אימורים can join to make one כזית. The meat of שלמים is eaten, not burned, so it seems it cannot join with the אימורים. The גמרא now has this inference ready to test.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings, whose meat is eaten
Yes
No
Etc.: the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: One who offers up an olive-bulk from the burnt offering, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 2: a כזית made of the עולה's meat together with its אימורים.

phrases.english: A burnt offering and its sacrificial parts – yes,
peace offerings and their sacrificial parts – no;

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלָה וְאֵימוּרֶיהָ – אִין, שְׁלָמִים וְאֵימוּרֵיהֶן – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and returns to the משנה of Step 2 to draw an inference from its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה's wording: the meat and אימורים of an עולה join to make a כזית for liability outside, but the meat and אימורים of שלמים do not.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing as our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that our משנה teaches what a ברייתא says outright: the meat and אימורים of an עולה combine to a כזית for offering outside, and for פיגול, נותר and טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה teaches what the Sages taught in a ברייתא: the meat of an עולה and its sacrificial parts add up together to make a כזית. This counts for offering them outside, and for being liable for eating them as פיגול, as נותר, or while טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says outright what it just learned from the משנה: only an עולה's meat and אימורים combine to a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the גמרא learned from the משנה that this combining works for an עולה but not for שלמים. Here a ברייתא says the same thing about the עולה. The ברייתא also adds a new point: the combining counts for פיגול, נותר and טמא too, not only for offering outside.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of an animal that are burned on the altar
They combine and add up to the minimum amount
An offering made invalid by a wrong thought about its proper time
Meat left over after the time allowed for eating it
Ritually impure; here, eating קדשים while impure

phrases.english: We have learned that which the Sages taught:
phrases.notes: Our משנה already teaches what this ברייתא says outright.

phrases.english: A burnt offering and its sacrificial parts combine to make an olive-bulk
for offering them up outside,
and to make one liable for them because of piggul,
notar, and impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 9's inference from the משנה with a ברייתא that says the same thing outright.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only an עולה's meat and אימורים combine to a כזית
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of the Sages (תנו רבנן)

steps.title: Why would פיגול, נותר and טמא depend on the עולה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why only an עולה combines for offering outside, but asks why the עולה would be special for פיגול, נותר and טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for offering outside: an עולה is burned completely, so everything combines, but שלמים are not. But for פיגול, נותר and טמא, what is the reason to make a difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: one half of its rule makes sense, but the other half seems to have no reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה goes completely on the altar, so its meat and אימורים are all 'altar material' and can add up for offering outside. שלמים meat is eaten, not burned, so it does not join the אימורים for that. But the sins of פיגול, נותר and טמא are about eating, and that reason has nothing to do with them, so why should only the עולה combine?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (opening a 'this part is fine, but...' challenge)
Burned entirely on the altar
Peace offerings, most of whose meat is eaten
What is the reason?

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding offering up a burnt offering –
since it is burned entirely, yes, it combines;
peace offerings, no;
but piggul, notar, and impurity –
what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why should the עולה be different from שלמים for these eating sins?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הַעֲלָאַת עוֹלָה דְּכָלִיל אִין שְׁלָמִים לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the second half of the ברייתא brought in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that only an עולה combines for פיגול, נותר and טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the difference (an עולה is fully burned) explains offering outside, but has nothing to do with sins of eating.

steps.title: A משנה says all פיגול and all נותר combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a contradiction: a משנה teaches that all פיגול combines and all נותר combines, with no limit to an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And didn't we learn in a משנה: All פיגול items combine, and all נותר items combine? So the ברייתא on פיגול clashes with the משנה on פיגול, and the ברייתא on נותר clashes with the משנה on נותר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the question stronger: it is not just 'why?', but a משנה actually says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (in מעילה) says 'all' פיגול and 'all' נותר combine, so this seems to include שלמים too. The ברייתא suggested only an עולה combines. Now there are two clear contradictions: one about פיגול and one about נותר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; there is a contradiction
Against, on (one ruling on פיגול against another)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
All piggul items combine,
and all notar items combine;
phrases.notes: The word 'all' sounds like it includes every kind of offering, not just an עולה.

phrases.english: so piggul contradicts piggul,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's rule on פיגול clashes with the משנה's rule on פיגול.

phrases.english: and notar contradicts notar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens step 11's question by bringing a משנה that seems to contradict the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's limit of combining for פיגול and נותר to an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in מעילה says all פיגול and all נותר combine, which sounds like it includes שלמים.

steps.title: Eating פיגול versus the thought that makes פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the פיגול contradiction: the משנה is about eating פיגול, while the ברייתא is about the thought that makes an offering פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction about פיגול is not difficult. Here (in the משנה) it is about eating פיגול; there (in the ברייתא) it is about the thought that makes something פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first of the two contradictions by showing that the two sources talk about different parts of פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once something is already פיגול, all פיגול pieces add up for the sin of eating, as the משנה says. The ברייתא is talking about the wrong thought that makes an offering פיגול in the first place, which needs a כזית. For that thought, only an עולה's meat and אימורים can join to make the כזית. The next step answers the contradiction about נותר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the contradiction is solved)
Here... there (each source is about a different case)
The wrong thought during the service that makes an offering פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up eating פיגול with making something פיגול. The משנה is about the sin of eating meat that is already פיגול. The ברייתא is about the thought during the service that turns the offering into פיגול.

phrases.english: Piggul against piggul is not difficult –
here it is about piggul itself,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה: it is about eating meat that is already פיגול.

phrases.english: there it is about the intention that makes piggul.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא: it is about the thought that turns the offering into פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: פִּיגּוּל אַפִּיגּוּל לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן בְּפִיגּוּל כָּאן בְּמַחְשֶׁבֶת פִּיגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half (פיגול) of the double contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different part of the law of פיגול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be about the same sin of eating פיגול, so they seemed to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about eating פיגול, where everything combines. The ברייתא is about the thought that makes פיגול, where only an עולה's meat and אימורים combine.

steps.title: The נותר contradiction is answered: eating versus what was left before sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about נותר is about eating it. The ברייתא is about an offering where only a כזית remained before the blood was sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction between the two rulings about נותר is not hard. Here (the משנה) it is about eating נותר. There (the ברייתא) it is about a case where only a little of the offering was left before the blood was sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the second half of the contradiction from Step 12, the part about נותר, the same way it answered פיגול in Step 13: the two sources are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule that all נותר combines is about eating נותר, and there the type of offering makes no difference. The ברייתא is about an offering where most of it was lost before the blood was sprinkled, and only a כזית made of meat and אימורים was left. Only for an עולה do these two parts combine to a כזית, which allows the blood to be sprinkled so the offering can later become נותר at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They were left over, meaning only that much of the offering remained.
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, the main act of the offering.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of 'left over' here. נוֹתָר is the forbidden meat left past its time. נִיתּוֹתְרוּ means only a small amount of the offering survived before the blood was sprinkled.

phrases.english: נותר against נותר is not difficult:
phrases.notes: This means the ברייתא's ruling on נותר seems to clash with the משנה's ruling on נותר from Step 12.

phrases.english: here, it is about eating נותר,
there, it is where only this much was left over
before the blood was sprinkled.
phrases.notes: Blood is only sprinkled if at least a כזית of the offering is left. Without sprinkling, the offering never becomes נותר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the נותר half of the contradiction, the same way Step 13 answered the פיגול half.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (אוקימתא): the two sources speak about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that only an עולה's parts combine to make someone liable for eating נותר, which goes against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For eating נותר, everything combines. The ברייתא's limit to an עולה is about whether a leftover כזית of meat plus אימורים allows the blood to be sprinkled.
steps.whyThisMatters: It removes the last contradiction. Now the ברייתא's 'only an עולה' rule fits with the משנה's 'all נותר combines.'

steps.title: Whose opinion is the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the ברייתא's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who taught the ברייתא as it has just been explained. This sets up the next step, where it names the תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא is read as being about whether a leftover כזית of meat and אימורים lets the blood be sprinkled. The גמרא wants to find a known תנא who holds that a leftover כזית makes the sprinkling valid.

keyTerms.meaning: And who is it? A question asking which תנא holds this view.

phrases.english: And who is it?
phrases.notes: He means: which תנא holds the view of the ברייתא as we just explained it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer in Step 14 by asking who holds that view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a leftover כזית matters for sprinkling the blood, as the ברייתא was just explained.

steps.title: It is רבי יהושע, and the גמרא begins quoting his ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יהושע. The גמרא starts quoting his ruling about all offerings where only a כזית of meat is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהושע. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע says, all the offerings in the תורה where only a כזית of meat is left...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is רבי יהושע's view. It begins quoting his ברייתא as proof, and the quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע is known for the view that if only a כזית of an offering is left, the blood may still be sprinkled. That fits the ברייתא as explained in Step 14. The rest of his words, which explain what happens with meat and אימורים, come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings.
Was left, meaning remained after the rest was lost.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehoshua;
as it is taught: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
All the offerings in the Torah
in which there remained an olive-bulk of meat

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא; דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15's question and begins bringing a source for that answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יהושע, who rules that a leftover כזית of an offering is enough to sprinkle the blood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי יהושע's ruling about all offerings where only a כזית of meat remained.
